name: Choose Region based on both business requirements and sustainability goals
guideline: Choose a Region for your workload based on both your business requirements and sustainability goals to optimize its KPIs, including performance, cost, and carbon footprint.

name: Scale workload infrastructure dynamically
guideline: Use elasticity of the cloud and scale your infrastructure dynamically to match supply of cloud resources to demand and avoid overprovisioned capacity in your workload.

name: Align SLAs with sustainability goals
guideline: Review and optimize workload service-level agreements (SLA) based on your sustainability goals to minimize the resources required to support your workload while continuing to meet business needs.

name:
Stop the creation and maintenance of unused
  assets
guideline: Decommission unused assets in your workload to reduce the number of cloud resources required to support your demand and minimize waste.

name: Optimize geographic placement of workloads based on their networking requirements
guideline: Select cloud location and services for your workload that reduce the distance network traffic must travel and decrease the total network resources required to support your workload.

name:
Optimize team member resources for activities
  performed
guideline: Optimize resources provided to team members to minimize the environmental sustainability impact while supporting their needs.

name: Implement buffering or throttling to flatten the demand curve
guideline: Buffering and throttling flatten the demand curve and reduce the provisioned capacity required for your workload.

name:
Optimize software and architecture for asynchronous
  and scheduled jobs
guideline: Use efficient software and architecture patterns such as queue-driven to maintain consistent high utilization of deployed resources.

name:
Remove or refactor workload components with low or
  no use
guideline: Remove components that are unused and no longer required, and refactor components with little utilization to minimize waste in your workload.

name:
Optimize areas of code that consume the most time or
  resources
guideline: Optimize your code that runs within different components of your architecture to minimize resource usage while maximizing performance.

name:
Optimize impact on devices and
  equipment
guideline: Understand the devices and equipment used in your architecture and use strategies to reduce their usage. This can minimize the overall environmental impact of your cloud workload.

name:
Use software patterns and architectures that best
  support data access and storage patterns
guideline: Understand how data is used within your workload, consumed by your users, transferred, and stored. Use software patterns and architectures that best support data access and storage to minimize the compute, networking, and storage resources required to support the workload.

name: Implement a data classification policy
guideline: Classify data to understand its criticality to business outcomes and choose the right energy-efficient storage tier to store the data.

name:
Use technologies that support data access and
  storage patterns
guideline: Use storage technologies that best support how your data is accessed and stored to minimize the resources provisioned while supporting your workload.

name: Use policies to manage the lifecycle of your datasets
guideline: Manage the lifecycle of all of your data and automatically enforce deletion to minimize the total storage required for your workload.

name: Use elasticity and automation to expand block storage or file system
guideline: Use elasticity and automation to expand block storage or file system as data grows to minimize the total provisioned storage.

name: Remove unneeded or redundant data
guideline: Remove unneeded or redundant data to minimize the storage resources required to store your datasets.

name:
Use shared file systems or storage to access
  common data
guideline: Adopt shared file systems or storage to avoid data duplication and allow for more efficient infrastructure for your workload.

name: Minimize data movement across networks
guideline: Use shared file systems or object storage to access common data and minimize the total networking resources required to support data movement for your workload.

name: Back up data only when difficult to recreate
guideline: Avoid backing up data that has no business value to minimize storage resources requirements for your workload.

name:
Use the minimum amount of hardware to meet your
  needs
guideline: Use the minimum amount of hardware for your workload to efficiently meet your business needs.

name: Use instance types with the least impact
guideline: Continually monitor and use new instance types to take advantage of energy efficiency improvements.

name: Use managed services
guideline: Use managed services to operate more efficiently in the cloud.

name: Optimize your use of hardware-based compute accelerators
guideline: Optimize your use of accelerated computing instances to reduce the physical infrastructure demands of your workload.

name: Communicate and cascade your sustainability goals
guideline: IT teams should clearly understand the organization's sustainability targets and work to communicate and cascade those priorities across its operations.

name:
Adopt methods that can rapidly introduce
  sustainability improvements
guideline: Adopt methods and processes to validate potential improvements, minimize testing costs, and deliver small improvements.

name: Keep your workload up-to-date
guideline: Keep your workload up-to-date to adopt efficient features, remove issues, and improve the overall efficiency of your workload.

name: Increase utilization of build environments
guideline: Increase the utilization of resources to develop, test, and build your workloads.

name: Use managed device farms for testing
guideline: Use managed device farms to efficiently test a new feature on a representative set of hardware.

name: Use circuit breaker patterns to stop repeated failing operations
guideline: Apply circuit breaker patterns to halt repeated failing operations, preventing unnecessary compute consumption during dependency failures.

name: Implement request throttling during overload conditions
guideline: Throttle requests during overload conditions to reduce cascading traffic amplification and backend stress.

name: Use graceful degradation patterns where possible
guideline: Apply graceful degradation so the system maintains partial functionality without triggering excessive recovery behavior.

name: Detect failure patterns early with monitoring and alerting
guideline: Detect failure patterns early through monitoring and alerting to reduce prolonged inefficient operation and speed recovery.

name: Design workloads to isolate dependency failures
guideline: Design workloads so dependency failures are isolated, preventing localized issues from propagating across the system.

name: Align resiliency architecture to defined business continuity requirements
guideline: Align resiliency architecture with actual business continuity requirements to avoid unnecessary always-on infrastructure and idle redundancy.

name: Evaluate whether multi-region deployments are truly required
guideline: Evaluate whether multi-region deployments are truly necessary, since unneeded ones add continuous replication traffic and duplicated infrastructure.

name: Assess monolith versus microservice tradeoffs carefully
guideline: Carefully weigh monolith versus microservice tradeoffs to avoid unnecessary service-to-service traffic and platform duplication.

name: Right-size failover environments instead of mirroring peak production scale
guideline: Right-size failover environments rather than mirroring peak production scale, minimizing standby infrastructure while still meeting recovery objectives.

name: Regularly review backup, replication, and retention strategies
guideline: Regularly review backup, replication, and retention strategies to reduce excessive data duplication and long-term storage growth.

name: Use asynchronous processing for burst-prone operations
guideline: Use asynchronous processing for burst-prone operations to smooth workload demand and reduce short-lived scale spikes.

name: Implement buffering and queue-based workload management
guideline: Implement buffering and queue-based workload management to stabilize infrastructure utilization over time.

name: Batch non-urgent operations where appropriate
guideline: Batch non-urgent operations where appropriate to improve compute efficiency by cutting repeated processing overhead.

name: Tune autoscaling policies to avoid aggressive short-term scaling reactions
guideline: Tune autoscaling policies to avoid aggressive short-term scaling reactions that expand infrastructure unnecessarily during temporary spikes.

name: Evaluate managed PaaS and serverless services where appropriate
guideline: Evaluate managed PaaS and serverless services where appropriate to improve infrastructure utilization through shared platform efficiency and reduce operational overhead.

name: Keep platform services, runtimes, and dependencies updated
guideline: Keep platform services, runtimes, and dependencies up to date to benefit from ongoing platform efficiency and reliability improvements.

name: Match service tiers and scalability models to actual workload demand
guideline: Match service tiers and scalability models to actual workload demand to prevent overprovisioning and idle infrastructure.

name: Remove zombie workloads, orphaned resources, and inactive environments regularly
guideline: Regularly remove zombie workloads, orphaned resources, and inactive environments that consume resources without delivering business value.

name: Shut down non-production environments when not in use
guideline: Shut down non-production environments when they're not in use to reduce unnecessary compute consumption and idle platform capacity.

name: Avoid dedicated infrastructure allocations unless workload requirements justify them
guideline: Avoid dedicated infrastructure allocations unless workload requirements truly justify them, maximizing use of shared hyperscale infrastructure.

name: Tune autoscaling behavior to avoid aggressive short-term scaling reactions
guideline: Tune autoscaling behavior to avoid aggressive short-term scaling reactions, stabilizing utilization and reducing unnecessary scale churn.

name: Use Spot VMs only for interrupt-tolerant workloads
guideline: Use Spot VMs only for interrupt-tolerant workloads to improve infrastructure utilization without introducing avoidable reliability instability.

name: Choose regions close to users when latency affects workload reliability
guideline: Choose regions close to users when latency affects workload reliability, reducing network traversal overhead and improving request stability.

name: Evaluate carbon intensity, latency, and resiliency tradeoffs together when selecting deployment regions
guideline: Weigh carbon intensity, latency, and resiliency together when selecting deployment regions to balance sustainability with reliability and user experience.

name: Use load testing and chaos engineering to assess how the workload behaves under outages, traffic spikes, and traffic dips
guideline: Use load testing and chaos engineering to see how the workload behaves under outages and traffic spikes or dips, improving resilience and reducing waste during real failures.

name: Use chaos engineering to simulate conditions that increase energy usage and identify inefficient execution paths
guideline: Use chaos engineering to simulate conditions that raise energy usage, exposing inefficient execution paths and supporting resource optimization under stress.

name: Define expected system behavior under constrained or inefficient operating conditions
guideline: Define how the system should behave under stress or constrained conditions to ensure predictable recovery and avoid prolonged inefficient operating states.

name: Consider implementing an eco version of the application that reduces features or performance to minimize energy usage
guideline: Consider building a reduced-feature "eco version" of the application as a benchmark for measuring and continuously optimizing energy usage.

name: Evaluate the tradeoff of running chaos engineering and load tests, since these activities themselves consume additional compute and increase emissions
guideline: Weigh the resource cost of chaos engineering and load testing against their benefits, since testing itself consumes compute and adds emissions.

name: Schedule and scope chaos engineering intentionally to balance resilience validation with the environmental cost of testing
guideline: Schedule and scope chaos engineering intentionally to balance resilience validation against the environmental cost of running tests.

name: Block malicious traffic as early as possible by using edge or network-level controls
guideline: Block malicious traffic as early as possible with edge or network-level controls to reduce compute and network usage from unwanted requests.

name: Use rate limiting and throttling to control excessive or abusive request patterns
guideline: Apply rate limiting and throttling to control abusive request patterns, preventing workload overload and unnecessary scaling events.

name: Apply identity-based access controls to restrict unauthorized usage
guideline: Apply identity-based access controls to restrict unauthorized usage and reduce processing of invalid or malicious requests.

name: Design security layers to filter traffic early rather than at application level
guideline: Design security layers to filter traffic early rather than at the application level, minimizing downstream resource consumption.

name: Avoid excessive overlapping security layers unless required
guideline: Avoid excessive overlapping security layers unless truly required, to reduce redundant processing and infrastructure overhead.

name: Harden networking components to reduce exposure and filter unwanted traffic early
guideline: Harden networking components to reduce exposure and filter unwanted traffic early, lowering network and compute usage from malicious requests.

name: Harden identity and access controls to ensure only legitimate usage patterns are allowed
guideline: Harden identity and access controls so only legitimate usage is allowed, reducing wasted processing from unauthorized activity.

name: Harden cloud resource configurations to eliminate weak points and misconfigurations
guideline: Harden cloud resource configurations to eliminate weak points and misconfigurations, preventing exploitation-driven workload spikes.

name: Harden application and code assets to prevent vulnerabilities from being exploited
guideline: Harden application and code assets to prevent exploited vulnerabilities from causing resource-heavy attack patterns and unstable execution.

name: Harden operational and management access paths to reduce administrative misuse or accidental impact
guideline: Harden operational and management access paths to reduce administrative misuse or accidental impact, improving stability and reducing unnecessary operational load.

name: Filter logs before ingestion into SIEM systems
guideline: Filter logs before they're ingested into SIEM systems to reduce unnecessary data processing, storage, and network transfer.

name: Collect only security signals required for detection and analysis
guideline: Collect only the security signals required for detection and analysis to minimize telemetry volume and avoid processing unused data.

name: Use cloud-native data collection rules to control and refine telemetry intake
guideline: Use cloud-native data collection rules to control and refine telemetry intake, preventing over-collection and continuous ingestion overhead.

name: Avoid forwarding full raw datasets when aggregated or filtered signals are sufficient
guideline: Avoid forwarding full raw datasets when aggregated or filtered signals suffice, reducing cross-system data movement and resource use.

name: Design security monitoring pipelines with purpose, not full-fidelity collection by default
guideline: Design security monitoring pipelines with a clear purpose rather than collecting full-fidelity data by default, lowering compute and storage demand while keeping required visibility.

name: Apply security controls closer to the source of traffic instead of relying on centralized inspection paths
guideline: Apply security controls closer to the traffic source instead of relying solely on centralized inspection paths, reducing unnecessary network traversal.

name: Avoid hub-and-spoke routing for traffic that does not require centralized inspection
guideline: Avoid hub-and-spoke routing for traffic that doesn't need centralized inspection, minimizing repeated data movement across network layers and regions.

name: Use cloud-native security services that enable local analysis and enforcement
guideline: Use cloud-native security services that enable local analysis and enforcement, reducing cross-system data transfer and improving network efficiency.

name: Design traffic flows to minimize intermediate hops introduced purely for security inspection
guideline: Design traffic flows to minimize intermediate hops added purely for security inspection, lowering bandwidth use and overall infrastructure load.

name: Track cost at the feature or workload level, not only at the infrastructure level
guideline: Track cost at the feature or workload level, not just infrastructure, to make hidden inefficiencies easier to find and address.

name: Use cost signals as one input to sustainability measurement
guideline: Use cost signals as one input to sustainability measurement, creating a practical basis for tracking improvement over time.

name: Define explicit efficiency baselines for critical systems
guideline: Define explicit efficiency baselines for critical systems to help teams detect drift before wasteful patterns become normal.

name: Treat observability spend as part of the optimization scope
guideline: Treat observability spend as part of the optimization scope to limit logging and telemetry growth that adds cost without enough value.

name: Assign cost accountability at the workload level
guideline: Assign cost accountability at the workload level to encourage end-to-end optimization instead of isolated local fixes.

name: Challenge local optimizations that shift cost elsewhere
guideline: Challenge local optimizations that merely shift cost elsewhere, improving system-wide efficiency rather than moving waste between teams.

name: Reduce API chattiness, payload size, and unnecessary repeat calls
guideline: Reduce API chattiness, payload size, and unnecessary repeat calls to lower avoidable compute demand and network transfer.

name: Prioritize algorithm and execution-path improvements in code that dominates runtime cost
guideline: Prioritize algorithm and execution-path improvements in the code that dominates runtime cost to reduce baseline CPU and memory consumption where it matters most.

name: Cache responses that are repeated, predictable, or expensive to regenerate
guideline: Cache responses that are repeated, predictable, or expensive to regenerate, preventing recomputation of work that adds no value.

name: Be cautious about adding abstraction in performance-critical paths
guideline: Be cautious about adding abstraction in performance-critical paths, since it limits execution overhead and coordination cost in hot paths.

name: Choose monolith or microservices based on real scaling and isolation needs
guideline: Choose monolith or microservices architecture based on real scaling and isolation needs, avoiding distributed-system overhead that doesn't improve outcomes.

name: Evaluate SSR and CSR choices against their total compute and transfer footprint
guideline: Evaluate server-side versus client-side rendering choices against their total compute and transfer footprint to reduce redundant rendering and data movement.

name: Remove cross-service data duplication and redundant domain models where possible
guideline: Remove cross-service data duplication and redundant domain models where possible to limit storage growth and compute amplification.

name: Auto-scale workloads against observed demand rather than assumed peak usage
guideline: Auto-scale workloads against observed demand rather than assumed peak usage to reduce persistent overprovisioning and idle capacity.

name: Shut down or downsize non-production environments when they are not needed
guideline: Shut down or downsize non-production environments when they aren't needed to remove baseline consumption that delivers no business value.

name: Remove orphaned and zombie resources on a regular cadence
guideline: Remove orphaned and zombie resources on a regular cadence to prevent silent cost accumulation from forgotten infrastructure.

name: Match platform tiers and reservations to actual usage patterns
guideline: Match platform tiers and reservations to actual usage patterns to avoid paying for oversized infrastructure by default.

name: Favor containers, PaaS, or serverless when they fit the workload
guideline: Favor containers, PaaS, or serverless options when they fit the workload, improving utilization through more efficient shared platform capacity.

name: Use Spot VMs only where interruption is acceptable and recovery is understood
guideline: Use Spot VMs only where interruption is acceptable and recovery is well understood, using spare capacity efficiently without added operational risk.

name: Optimize CI/CD pipelines with caching, reuse, and incremental builds
guideline: Optimize CI/CD pipelines with caching, reuse, and incremental builds to cut redundant compute execution in engineering workflows.

name: Consider lower-carbon regions as part of workload placement decisions
guideline: Factor lower-carbon regions into workload placement decisions to reduce emissions per unit of compute when other requirements still hold.

name: Schedule batch workloads to take advantage of lower-carbon or lower-cost periods
guideline: Schedule batch workloads to run during lower-carbon or lower-cost periods, aligning flexible compute with cleaner operating windows.

name: Place workloads closer to users when latency and transfer patterns justify it
guideline: Place workloads closer to users when latency and transfer patterns justify it, reducing network distance and unnecessary transfer cost.

name: Avoid cross-region routing and replication that do not serve a clear workload need
guideline: Avoid cross-region routing and replication that don't serve a clear workload need, lowering network overhead and duplicated infrastructure activity.

name: Reassess regional deployment choices against actual usage over time
guideline: Periodically reassess regional deployment choices against actual usage to prevent static placement decisions from becoming long-term inefficiencies.

name: Use CDNs for content that is requested repeatedly at scale
guideline: Use CDNs for content requested repeatedly at scale to reduce origin compute demand and repeated network delivery.

name: Compress payloads and choose transfer formats with care
guideline: Compress payloads and choose transfer formats carefully to lower bandwidth consumption without changing business outcomes.

name: Reduce cross-service chaining and fan-out from a single user action
guideline: Reduce cross-service chaining and fan-out triggered by a single user action to prevent request amplification from multiplying backend work.

name: Keep traffic within regional boundaries when the architecture allows it
guideline: Keep traffic within regional boundaries when the architecture allows it, avoiding expensive and unnecessary cross-region routing.

name: Place workloads near users when delivery patterns make that worthwhile
guideline: Place workloads near users when delivery patterns make it worthwhile, minimizing transfer distance and helping control latency-related overhead.

name: Centralize media processing when the same transformations would otherwise be repeated
guideline: Centralize media processing when the same transformations would otherwise be repeated, reducing duplicated encoding and transformation work.

name: Match storage tiers to how often data is actually accessed
guideline: Match storage tiers to how often data is actually accessed to reduce infrastructure cost tied to over-served data.

name: Remove stale, redundant, or low-value data on purpose
guideline: Actively remove stale, redundant, or low-value data to lower the long-term storage footprint without reducing useful capability.

name: Control logging and telemetry growth before retention becomes passive sprawl
guideline: Control logging and telemetry growth before retention becomes passive sprawl, preventing ingestion and storage costs from outpacing their value.

name: Avoid duplicating datasets across services unless there is a clear reason
guideline: Avoid duplicating datasets across services unless there's a clear reason, reducing storage growth and repeated processing of the same data.

name: Review backup retention policies against actual recovery requirements
guideline: Review backup retention policies against actual recovery requirements to eliminate redundant long-term storage that doesn't improve resilience.

name: Compress stored data where the tradeoff is favorable
guideline: Compress stored data where the tradeoff is favorable to reduce storage footprint and transfer volume with limited downside.

name: Scale CI/CD resources dynamically instead of keeping capacity always available
guideline: Scale CI/CD resources dynamically instead of keeping capacity always available, preventing idle compute waste between engineering events.

name: Cache build artifacts aggressively where reuse is reliable
guideline: Cache build artifacts aggressively where reuse is reliable to avoid repeated computation for unchanged inputs.

name: Run tests for changed components when full-suite execution is not necessary
guideline: Run tests only for changed components when full-suite execution isn't necessary, reducing compute spent on validation that adds little signal.

name: Introduce incremental build strategies where tooling supports them well
guideline: Introduce incremental build strategies where tooling supports them well, limiting unnecessary full-system recomputation.

name: Remove redundant pipeline stages and duplicate checks
guideline: Remove redundant pipeline stages and duplicate checks to lower the total compute footprint of delivery workflows.

name: Avoid always-on full-suite testing when risk does not justify it
guideline: Avoid always-on full-suite testing when the risk doesn't justify it, reducing baseline CI/CD cost without losing meaningful validation.

name: Establish a baseline of current carbon emissions for all workloads and services
guideline: Establish a baseline of current carbon emissions across workloads and services to provide a reference point for measuring improvement over time.

name: Use emissions monitoring tools such as the Azure Carbon Optimizer to track environmental impact
guideline: Use emissions monitoring tools such as the Azure Carbon Optimizer to enable data-driven decisions and identify the largest sources of emissions.

name: Define carbon reduction targets for the workload and individual workload components
guideline: Define carbon reduction targets for the workload and its individual components to create clear objectives and drive accountability.

name: Track sustainability using a combination of factors and a measurable metric such as an SCI score
guideline: Track sustainability through a combination of performance, carbon emissions, and cost proxies, developing a measurable metric (such as a Software Carbon Intensity score) and SLOs/SLAs to give a holistic view of workload efficiency.

name: Record and assess the impact of all sustainability-related changes and optimizations
guideline: Record and assess the impact of every sustainability-related change to build an evidence-based view of the most effective reduction strategies.

name: Follow organizational governance to enforce sustainability outcomes in workload teams
guideline: Follow organizational governance to enforce sustainability outcomes across workload teams, establishing consistent practices and reducing variability.

name: Use existing cost governance controls and policies as part of sustainability initiatives
guideline: Reuse existing cost governance controls and policies as part of sustainability initiatives to reduce unnecessary resource consumption and lower emissions.

name: Utilize built-in Azure Policy controls to enforce efficient resource configurations and operational standards
guideline: Use built-in Azure Policy controls to enforce efficient resource configurations and operational standards, promoting ongoing cloud efficiency.

name: Create a dedicated sustainability-focused Azure Policy initiative
guideline: Create a dedicated sustainability-focused Azure Policy initiative to embed sustainability into workload design, deployment, and operations.

name: Implement data lifecycle management policies to ensure only necessary data is collected, retained, and processed
guideline: Implement data lifecycle management policies (for example, using Microsoft Purview for classification and retention, and Azure Monitor Data Collection Rules to control telemetry) so only necessary data is collected and retained, reducing storage, transfer, and processing overhead.

name: Regularly review policy compliance and identify opportunities for further optimization
guideline: Regularly review policy compliance and look for further optimization opportunities to sustain long-term efficiency gains.

name: Establish a sustainability community or center of excellence responsible for promoting cloud efficiency and green software practices
guideline: Establish a sustainability community or center of excellence to create organizational ownership and consistently drive green software practices.

name: Provide ongoing sustainability and green software training for architects, developers, and operations teams
guideline: Provide ongoing sustainability and green software training for architects, developers, and operations teams to improve environmentally responsible decision-making.

name: Define sustainability policies, targets, and expectations, and communicate them regularly across the organization
guideline: Define sustainability policies, targets, and expectations, and communicate them regularly to align teams around common objectives.

name: Create a centralized repository for sustainability guidance, best practices, and lessons learned
guideline: Create a centralized repository of sustainability guidance and lessons learned to accelerate adoption and reduce duplicated effort.

name: Encourage regular knowledge-sharing sessions, workshops, or internal webinars focused on sustainability
guideline: Encourage regular knowledge-sharing sessions or webinars on sustainability to promote continuous learning and scale successful initiatives.

name: Include sustainability metrics and objectives as part of workload governance, performance reviews, or KPIs
guideline: Include sustainability metrics and objectives in workload governance, performance reviews, or KPIs to embed them into decision-making.

name: Recognize and reward teams that achieve sustainability goals through incentives, gamification, or certifications
guideline: Recognize and reward teams that achieve sustainability goals through incentives, gamification, or certifications to encourage continued participation.

name: Promote carbon-aware and carbon-optimized application design practices across all workload teams
guideline: Promote carbon-aware and carbon-optimized application design practices across all workload teams to reduce emissions over time.

name: Optimize API communication patterns by reducing chatty interactions, minimizing payload sizes, and using efficient message encoding techniques
guideline: Optimize API communication by reducing chatty interactions, minimizing payload size, and using efficient encoding to cut network traffic and energy use.

name: Implement request throttling and response caching by using services such as Azure API Management
guideline: Implement request throttling and response caching (for example with Azure API Management) to prevent unnecessary and repeated backend processing.

name: Monitor API usage patterns and continuously optimize high-volume or inefficient endpoints
guideline: Monitor API usage patterns and continuously optimize high-volume or inefficient endpoints to reduce resource utilization and carbon footprint.

name: Evaluate rendering strategies and select server-side or client-side rendering based on user device capabilities, network conditions, and workload requirements
guideline: Choose server-side or client-side rendering based on device capabilities, network conditions, and workload needs to optimize compute utilization across client and server.

name: Leverage caching mechanisms, whether centralized on the server or within the browser, to minimize repeated rendering and data processing operations
guideline: Use server-side or browser caching to minimize repeated rendering and data processing, reducing compute and network resource use.

name: Design lightweight and efficient user interfaces by minimizing unnecessary components, pages, and media assets
guideline: Design lightweight, efficient user interfaces with minimal unnecessary components and media assets to reduce network traffic and compute use.

name: Optimize content delivery by using appropriately sized images and videos, avoiding unnecessary asset downloads, and leveraging system fonts where practical
guideline: Optimize content delivery with appropriately sized media, avoid unnecessary asset downloads, and use system fonts where practical to lower bandwidth and client-side processing.

name: Improve user navigation and findability, and consider offering resource-efficient experiences such as simplified interfaces or dark mode options
guideline: Improve navigation and findability, and consider resource-efficient experiences such as simplified interfaces or dark mode, to reduce unnecessary data retrieval and energy use.

name: Profile workloads to understand concurrency patterns, resource utilization, and opportunities for performance optimization or parallelization
guideline: Profile workloads to understand concurrency and resource utilization, uncovering opportunities for optimization or parallelization that improve compute efficiency.

name: Evaluate specialized compute options, such as GPU-based resources, where they provide efficiency gains
guideline: Evaluate specialized compute options such as GPUs where they provide genuine efficiency gains, balancing performance benefit against higher operational cost.

name: Establish CPU and memory baselines and incorporate sustainability-focused testing, monitoring, alerts, and quality gates into deployment pipelines
guideline: Establish CPU and memory baselines and build sustainability-focused testing, monitoring, and quality gates into deployment pipelines to catch inefficient code before production.

name: Use content delivery networks (CDNs), caching strategies, including in-memory caching where appropriate, and data compression techniques to reduce network traffic and optimize content delivery
guideline: Use CDNs, caching strategies (including in-memory caching), and data compression to reduce network traffic and optimize content delivery.

name: Deploy workloads and content closer to users and keep dependent resources within the same cloud and region where practical
guideline: Deploy workloads and content closer to users and keep dependent resources within the same cloud and region where practical, minimizing network traversal.

name: Regularly review and tune caching configurations, such as cache retention and expiration settings, to maximize efficiency and resource utilization
guideline: Regularly review and tune caching configurations, such as retention and expiration settings, to maximize cache effectiveness and reduce unnecessary data transfer.

name: Apply storage compression, optimize database queries, and reduce unnecessary data transfer to improve storage efficiency and performance
guideline: Apply storage compression, optimize database queries, and reduce unnecessary data transfer to lower storage capacity needs and processing overhead.

name: Align data with appropriate storage access tiers and lifecycle policies, ensuring frequently accessed data is kept in hot storage while infrequently accessed data is moved to cold or archive storage
guideline: Align data with appropriate storage tiers and lifecycle policies, keeping hot data readily accessible while moving infrequently used data to cold or archive storage.

name: Implement and regularly review backup, recovery point, and log retention policies using services such as Azure Backup and Azure Monitor to prevent unnecessary data accumulation
guideline: Implement and regularly review backup, recovery-point, and log retention policies (for example with Azure Backup and Azure Monitor) to prevent unnecessary long-term data accumulation.

name: Review platform and service tier decisions to ensure they align with actual workload demand and resource utilization patterns
guideline: Review platform and service tier decisions against actual workload demand and utilization patterns to reduce underutilized compute capacity.

name: Prefer services and architectures that support dynamic scaling based on demand rather than fixed provisioned capacity
guideline: Prefer services and architectures that scale dynamically with demand rather than relying on fixed provisioned capacity, minimizing idle compute.

name: Evaluate whether higher-tier services are necessary for required features, and avoid overprovisioning where possible
guideline: Evaluate whether higher-tier services are truly necessary for required features and avoid overprovisioning where possible.

name: Implement caching in CI/CD pipelines to store and reuse build outputs and artifacts between runs when inputs don't change
guideline: Cache build outputs and artifacts in CI/CD pipelines for reuse between runs when inputs are unchanged, reducing repeated compute cycles.

name: Use local caching on self-hosted CI/CD agents where possible to minimize network transfers and external data movement
guideline: Use local caching on self-hosted CI/CD agents where possible to minimize network transfers and external data movement.

name: Identify and modernize legacy applications by migrating to modern cloud-native architectures such as serverless or optimized PaaS services
guideline: Identify and modernize legacy applications by migrating to cloud-native architectures such as serverless or optimized PaaS, improving compute efficiency.

name: Keep platforms, services, and operating systems up to date by using automated update mechanisms such as Azure Automation Update Management
guideline: Keep platforms, services, and operating systems up to date using automated update mechanisms so workloads benefit from the latest efficiency improvements.

name: Understand the carbon intensity of cloud regions
guideline: Learn how the Carbon-Free Energy (CFE) percentage metric measures the share of clean energy powering each region's grid on an hourly basis, so this data can inform region choices.

name: Incorporate CFE in your location-selection strategy
guideline: Favor the cleanest available region for long-running workloads using the region picker's low-CO2 indicator, and enforce the choice with Organization Policy resource-location constraints.

name: Use time-of-day scheduling
guideline: Shift flexible, compute-intensive workloads such as training and batch inference to run when the local grid's carbon-free energy share is highest, cutting emissions without sacrificing performance.

name: Architect for energy efficiency by using TPUs
guideline: Use Tensor Processing Units, purpose-built AI accelerators with higher computation per watt than general-purpose hardware, to cut energy use across training, inference, and cooling.

name: Follow the 4Ms best practices for resource selection
guideline: Apply the Model, Machine, Mechanization, and Map framework -- efficient models, optimized processors, cloud deployment, and low-carbon regions -- to substantially cut the carbon footprint of ML workloads.

name: Select efficient AI models
guideline: Default to the smallest model that meets accuracy requirements, such as a distilled variant, instead of automatically reaching for the largest available model.

name: Use domain-specific, hyper-efficient solutions
guideline: Prefer specialized, pretrained models built for a narrow domain, such as geospatial or weather forecasting, over general-purpose foundation models, since they need far less compute.

name: Apply appropriate model compression techniques
guideline: Reduce model size and energy use through pruning, quantization, or knowledge distillation while preserving acceptable accuracy.

name: Use specialized hardware
guideline: Run training and inference on accelerators purpose-built for ML rather than general-purpose processors to gain multi-fold improvements in performance per watt.

name: Use parameter-efficient fine-tuning
guideline: Fine-tune large models with techniques like LoRA that freeze most weights and train only small additional layers, cutting the cost and energy of adaptation versus full fine-tuning.

name: Optimize model training processes
guideline: Reduce wasted training compute with early stopping once validation performance plateaus, efficient data pipelines that keep accelerators fed, and smarter hyperparameter search such as Bayesian optimization.

name: Improve inference efficiency
guideline: Batch inference requests for parallel processing and use multi-layer caching, including key-value and semantic caches, to avoid recomputing results.

name: Measure and monitor
guideline: Track token usage, energy consumption, and carbon footprint of AI workloads, and monitor production models for drift so optimizations can be correlated with impact.

name: Implement carbon-aware scheduling
guideline: Run resource-intensive ML pipeline jobs in the cleanest available regions and during the times when the local grid has the most carbon-free energy.

name: Optimize data pipelines
guideline: Use managed data-processing services such as Dataflow or Managed Service for Apache Spark to prepare training data efficiently, so expensive compute isn't left idle waiting on data.

name: Embrace MLOps
guideline: Automate the ML lifecycle so models are continuously monitored, validated, and redeployed only when needed, avoiding unnecessary retraining.

name: Use managed services
guideline: Offload resource management to managed AI platforms that provide built-in hyperparameter tuning and resource optimization, reducing the overhead of running efficient infrastructure yourself.

name: Use horizontal scaling
guideline: Scale out by adding instances rather than scaling up a single instance's size, since horizontal scaling distributes load more efficiently and adapts better to variable demand.

name: Configure appropriate scaling policies
guideline: Base autoscaling on custom metrics and thresholds tailored to the application rather than CPU utilization alone, to avoid scaling thrash and overprovisioning.

name: Combine reactive and proactive scaling
guideline: Pair reactive autoscaling for unpredictable spikes with scheduled autoscaling for known, predictable demand patterns.

name: Design stateless applications
guideline: Keep session state in an external store, such as Redis, rather than on the compute instance itself, so instances can be added or removed freely during scaling.

name: Schedule for low carbon intensity
guideline: Time batch jobs to run in cleaner regions and during periods of abundant renewable energy, using the Carbon Footprint report to find optimal windows.

name: Use Spot VMs for noncritical workloads
guideline: Run fault-tolerant, non-critical batch jobs on discounted Spot VM capacity instead of provisioning dedicated resources.

name: Consolidate and parallelize jobs
guideline: Group similar jobs into larger batches, for example with Batch, to reduce per-job startup and shutdown overhead and keep infrastructure better utilized.

name: Use managed services
guideline: Let services like Batch and Dataflow provision and scale resources automatically based on workload volume, eliminating idle capacity.

name: Match VM machine families to workload requirements
guideline: Pick the machine family -- general-purpose, compute-, memory-, storage-, or accelerator-optimized -- that best fits the workload's actual resource profile.

name: Upgrade to the latest machine types
guideline: Move to newer processor generations with better power management and higher performance-per-watt to cut both energy use and task completion time.

name: Leverage the scale-to-zero capability of Cloud Run
guideline: Deploy intermittent or event-driven services on Cloud Run so they scale down to zero instances when idle, eliminating energy waste from unused capacity.

name: Automate resource optimization using GKE
guideline: Use GKE's bin packing, horizontal and vertical pod autoscaling, and topology-aware scheduling to maximize node utilization and cut wasted energy.

name: Configure carbon-aware scheduling
guideline: Combine geographic shifting to cleaner regions with temporal shifting to periods of higher renewable availability, guided by real-time grid carbon-intensity data.

name: Optimize for cold start efficiency
guideline: Keep disaster-recovery resources turned off or scaled to zero, use serverless failover, and automate recovery via infrastructure-as-code instead of maintaining always-on warm standby capacity.

name: Balance redundancy and utilization
guideline: Prefer active-active architectures over active-passive, and replicate data only when genuinely required, so redundant systems don't sit idle wasting energy.

name: Eliminate redundant logic and feature bloat
guideline: Implement only the functionality that provides measurable user value, and regularly audit applications to find and remove features that add computational overhead without real benefit.

name: Refactor
guideline: Periodically revisit and simplify code that has accumulated unused branches or dead paths, rather than letting inefficiencies persist indefinitely.

name: Avoid unnecessary operations
guideline: Defer computation until a result is actually needed, using techniques like lazy evaluation so unused work is never performed.

name: Prioritize code readability and reusability
guideline: Follow the DRY principle and write clear, reusable code to minimize duplicated logic, which also reduces the effort -- and associated emissions -- of ongoing development and maintenance.

name: Cache frequent data
guideline: Keep frequently accessed data in a fast, temporary store such as Memorystore to cut down on repeated database queries and disk I/O.

name: Cache API responses
guideline: Cache the results of frequent API calls to avoid repeating the same costly network requests and computation.

name: Prioritize in-memory caching
guideline: Favor high-speed RAM-based caches over persistent storage to sidestep slow disk I/O and complex database lookups.

name: Select appropriate cache-write strategies
guideline: Choose write-through caching to boost cache-hit rates and cut reads, or write-back caching for write-heavy workloads to reduce immediate database load.

name: Use smart eviction policies
guideline: Apply TTL, LRU, or LFU eviction so stale entries are removed and cache space stays available for the data that's actually being requested.

name: Focus on reducing complexity
guideline: Evaluate an algorithm's theoretical time and space complexity, not just observed runtime, when choosing an approach that minimizes resource consumption.

name: Avoid redundant work
guideline: Rely on built-in, language- or framework-optimized functions, typically implemented in efficient lower-level languages, instead of reimplementing common operations.

name: Optimize for search and retrieval
guideline: Use hash maps or hash sets for near-constant-time lookups instead of linear searches through arrays, cutting the energy spent per query.

name: Minimize memory footprint
guideline: Choose compact, efficient data structures to shrink an application's memory usage, which lowers power consumption and delays the need for hardware upgrades.

name: Use specialized structures
guideline: Apply purpose-built structures, such as tries for prefix searches or priority queues for min/max access, when they fit the access pattern better than general-purpose collections.

name: Prefer event-driven logic over polling
guideline: Replace busy-wait loops or periodic polling with event-driven triggers so processing only happens on demand.

name: Prevent constant high frequency
guideline: Avoid code patterns that force the CPU to run continuously at maximum frequency, so idle systems can drop into low-power states.

name: Use asynchronous processing
guideline: Use async processing so threads aren't blocked waiting on I/O, freeing compute resources for other work and improving overall utilization.

name: Strict memory management
guideline: Proactively release memory that's no longer needed rather than holding large objects longer than necessary, to avoid resource bottlenecks.

name: Optimize disk I/O
guideline: Buffer writes in memory and flush to persistent storage at set intervals or size thresholds rather than performing frequent small disk operations.

name: Batch operations
guideline: Consolidate many small disk reads and writes into fewer, larger batch operations, which consume less energy than numerous individual transactions.

name: Use compression
guideline: Apply suitable data-compression techniques, such as Cloud Storage's decompressive transcoding, to reduce the volume of data written to and read from disk.

name: Minimize payload size
guideline: Design APIs and applications to transfer only the fields a request actually needs, avoiding oversized JSON or XML payloads.

name: Reduce round-trips
guideline: Adopt more efficient protocols and patterns -- HTTP/3 over HTTP/1.1, GraphQL over REST, binary protocols, and consolidated API calls -- to cut the number of network round-trips.

name: Minimization and compression
guideline: Strip unnecessary characters from JavaScript, CSS, and HTML with minification tools, and compress images and other assets as part of the CI/CD pipeline.

name: Lazy loading
guideline: Load images, videos, and other non-critical assets only when they're about to be needed, such as when scrolled into view, to cut initial data transfer.

name: Smaller JavaScript bundles
guideline: Use modern bundlers and tree shaking to strip unused code out of JavaScript bundles, producing smaller, faster-loading files.

name: Browser caching
guideline: Set HTTP caching headers so browsers store static assets locally, avoiding repeated downloads and unnecessary network traffic on return visits.

name: Efficient rendering
guideline: Minimize frequent DOM manipulation and unnecessary re-rendering to keep client-side rendering lightweight.

name: Lightweight design patterns
guideline: Favor static sites or progressive web apps over heavier dynamic architectures, since they load faster and need fewer server resources.

name: Accessibility and performance
guideline: Build responsive, fast-loading, accessible sites, since accessible design and lean performance typically go hand in hand with lower resource consumption.

name: Identify and eliminate duplication
guideline: Set policies against needless dataset replication, using centralized, access-controlled repositories as the single source of truth.

name: Remove shadow data and dark data
guideline: Use discovery tooling to find unauthorized copies and data of unknown value, then archive or delete it appropriately.

name: Minimize the data volume for AI workloads
guideline: Use sampling, aggregation, and synthetic data generation to keep model performance while avoiding storage of unnecessarily large raw datasets.

name: Integrate data quality checks
guideline: Run automated validation and cleaning pipelines at ingestion so low-quality data doesn't waste storage and energy downstream.

name: Review the value density of data
guideline: Periodically assess high-volume datasets, like logs and IoT streams, to see whether aggregation or down-sampling can preserve useful information while shrinking storage footprint.

name: Critically evaluate the need for backups
guideline: Keep backups only for data that is unique or expensive to recreate, and avoid retaining copies of easily regenerated data such as intermediate ETL output or ephemeral caches.

name: Select an appropriate Cloud Storage class
guideline: Automate transitions of data to lower-carbon storage classes, such as Archive, based on how frequently it's accessed.

name: Implement aggressive data lifecycle policies
guideline: Define automated time-to-live rules for non-essential data such as logs and temporary artifacts so it's deleted automatically after a set period.

name: Mandate resource tagging
guideline: Require consistent labels on storage resources for ownership, purpose, and retention period, enabling automated lifecycle management and emissions reporting.

name: Right-size and deprovision compute storage
guideline: Regularly audit persistent disks for overprovisioning, delete unneeded snapshots, and apply retention policies to shrink underlying storage requirements.

name: Optimize the storage format
guideline: Use compressed, columnar formats such as Parquet instead of row-based formats to cut disk-space use and improve read efficiency.

name: Select low-carbon storage regions
guideline: Store data in regions with cleaner grids, and use Organization Policy constraints to prevent resource creation in high-carbon locations.

name: Minimize replication
guideline: Replicate data across regions only when required for disaster recovery or high availability, since cross-region replication meaningfully increases energy cost.

name: Optimize data processing locations
guideline: Run compute-intensive processing in the same region as the data it reads to avoid the energy cost of unnecessary cross-region network transfer.

name: Optimize data movement for your partners and customers
guideline: Direct partners toward efficient transfer methods like Storage Transfer Service and consider Requester Pays buckets so the environmental cost of transfers is attributed appropriately.

name: Grant permissions
guideline: Grant relevant teams the Carbon Footprint Viewer IAM role so they can access carbon emissions data in the Google Cloud console.

name: Automate data export
guideline: Structure the resource hierarchy to reflect business units and configure automated exports of Carbon Footprint data to BigQuery for deeper analysis and custom reporting.

name: Define carbon-related key performance indicators (KPIs)
guideline: Establish metrics that connect emissions to business value, such as CO2e per customer, transaction, or revenue unit.

name: Prioritize by scope
guideline: Break down Carbon Footprint data by project, region, and service to quickly find the largest sources of emissions.

name: Use dual-accounting
guideline: Evaluate regional carbon impact using both location-based emissions from the local grid and market-based emissions that reflect Google's carbon-free energy purchases.

name: Correlate with cost
guideline: Join carbon and billing data in BigQuery so optimization decisions can weigh sustainability and cost together rather than cost alone.

name: Annotate data to measure return on effort (ROE)
guideline: Tag carbon data with specific optimization events, such as a right-sizing change, so the resulting emissions reduction can be attributed to that action.

name: Decommission unattended projects
guideline: Use the unattended-project recommender alongside Carbon Footprint data to find and remove unused projects for immediate, verifiable emissions reduction.

name: Right-size resources
guideline: Apply Active Assist recommendations to match provisioned capacity to actual utilization, including choosing more efficient machine types for compute- and AI-heavy workloads.

name: Adopt carbon-aware scheduling
guideline: For batch workloads without strict timing needs, factor regional carbon-free energy data into scheduling and use Organization Policy to restrict new resources to low-carbon regions.

name: Reduce data sprawl
guideline: Apply data governance to move infrequently accessed data to cold storage or delete it outright, cutting storage-related energy use.

name: Refine application code
guideline: Address code-level inefficiencies that cause excessive resource use or unnecessary computation.

name: Implement GreenOps governance
guideline: Stand up a formal function that combines Carbon Footprint and Cloud Billing data in shared dashboards, embedding sustainability into regular operational reviews.

name: Use Carbon Footprint data for reporting and compliance
guideline: Use Google's verified, auditable carbon data to support ESG disclosures and other stakeholder transparency requirements.

name: Invest in training and awareness
guideline: Provide mandatory training so teams can access, interpret, and act on carbon data and optimization recommendations in their daily work.

name: Define carbon requirements
guideline: Add carbon-emission metrics as non-functional requirements in application acceptance criteria so low-carbon design is considered from the start of development.

name: Automate GreenOps
guideline: Use scripts, templates, and infrastructure-as-code to automatically apply Active Assist recommendations consistently across the organization.

name: Connect to the big picture
guideline: Help teams see how their architectural choices contribute to the organization's sustainability commitments, turning abstract carbon metrics into tangible progress indicators.

name: Communicate financial and sustainability goals
guideline: Share sustainability objectives and progress transparently across the organization, including in financial reporting, so technical teams see their work as tied to public commitments.

name: Embrace a shared fate mindset
guideline: Teach teams that Google manages the sustainability of the underlying cloud infrastructure while customers manage the sustainability of their own workloads, framing it as a shared partnership.

name: Provide role-based sustainability training
guideline: Tailor sustainability education by role -- compute intensity for data scientists, code efficiency for developers, region selection for architects, utilization for operations, and strategic alignment for leadership.

name: Empower managers to advocate for sustainability
guideline: Give managers the data and authority to weigh environmental impact alongside business metrics, so they can champion greener infrastructure choices.

name: Align with industry standards and frameworks
guideline: Ground sustainability efforts in recognized global and regional standards to keep them credible and measurable.

name: Define carbon KPIs and NFRs
guideline: Set specific, measurable sustainability targets, such as CO2 per request or per training run, and treat them as core technical requirements alongside latency and availability.

name: Measure return on effort
guideline: Help teams find high-impact, low-effort sustainability improvements by giving visibility into carbon avoided relative to the effort required.

name: Recognize and celebrate carbon reduction
guideline: Make sustainability wins visible across the organization through dashboards and recognition, to build momentum for continued progress.

name: W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines
guideline: Follow the W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines to build more energy-efficient websites and applications across the full lifecycle, from business strategy to infrastructure, reducing network traffic, client processing, and server load.

name: Green Software Foundation
guideline: Adopt the Green Software Foundation's Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) specification as a common standard for measuring a software system's carbon emissions rate.

name: Greenhouse Gas Protocol
guideline: Report emissions using the GHG Protocol, the widely adopted WRI/WBCSD standard for measuring, managing, and publicly disclosing greenhouse gas emissions, to keep sustainability data credible and auditable.

name: Adopt serverless architecture for AI/ML workload processes
guideline: Building an ML model takes significant computing resources that need to be optimized for efficient utilization; using serverless architecture for AI/ML workload processes helps match resource consumption to actual demand.

name: Choose the region that is closest to users
guideline: From an energy-efficiency perspective, it is better to shorten the distance a network packet travels so that less energy is required to transmit it, so choose the cloud region closest to your users.

name: Containerize your workloads
guideline: Containerizing workloads enables better resource utilisation and bin packing, reducing unnecessary compute allocation and embodied carbon.

name: Implement stateless design
guideline: Applications that consume large memory or on-disk data require larger VM sizes, especially for cloud computing, so designing components to be stateless allows them to be right-sized and scaled more efficiently.

name: Queue non-urgent processing requests
guideline: From a hardware-efficiency perspective, systems are more efficient when the impact of request spikes is minimised through even utilization, so non-urgent requests should be queued rather than processed immediately.

name: Run AI models at the edge
guideline: Deploy AI inference on edge devices or local infrastructure to reduce data transfer, network energy use, and reliance on centralised cloud compute.

name: Scale logical components independently
guideline: Decomposing applications into independently scalable microservices allows each component to be right-sized for its own demand, avoiding over-provisioning of the whole system.

name: Select efficient accelerators and instance types for AI workloads
guideline: Match AI workloads to the most energy-efficient hardware accelerator or instance type available to improve utilisation and reduce energy consumption.

name: Use on-demand execution for AI and agent workloads
guideline: Trigger AI and agent workloads only when needed using serverless or event-driven platforms to eliminate idle compute.

name: Evaluate other CPU architectures
guideline: Applications are built with a software architecture that best fits the business need they are serving; evaluating alternative CPU architectures (e.g. ARM) can improve energy efficiency for a given workload.

name: Use serverless cloud services
guideline: Serverless cloud services scale dynamically with demand and share infrastructure across many applications, improving overall utilization and reducing embodied carbon compared to dedicated infrastructure.

name: Prioritise system-first typography selection based on user needs
guideline: Align typography and component choices with actual user needs, preferring system fonts and existing assets over custom downloads to reduce unnecessary data transfer and rendering overhead.

name: Avoid an excessive DOM size
guideline: The greater the number of nodes defined in HTML, the greater the time spent processing and rendering each element, so keeping the DOM size small reduces energy used during rendering.

name: Avoid chaining critical requests
guideline: Most web experiences require a lot of work from the user's browser; the greater the length of request chains and the larger the download sizes, the more significant the impact on page load performance and the energy required to render a page.

name: Avoid tracking unnecessary data
guideline: User tracking, data collection and targeting in things like advertisements are responsible for significant energy use in many digital products and services, so only track data that is actually needed.

name: Cache static data
guideline: From an energy-efficiency perspective, it is better to reduce network traffic by reading data locally through a cache rather than accessing it remotely over the network.

name: Compress stored data
guideline: Storing uncompressed data wastes bandwidth and increases storage capacity requirements; applying appropriate compression reduces both.

name: Compress transmitted data
guideline: From an energy-efficiency perspective, it is better to minimise the size of the data transmitted so that less energy is required because network traffic is reduced.

name: Defer offscreen images
guideline: Web pages often include images that are not displayed on the first loaded screen and can thus be loaded dynamically (lazy-loaded) instead of upfront, reducing unnecessary data transfer.

name: Deprecate GIFs for animated content
guideline: A direct replacement for the GIF is the MP4 video format, which provides much smaller file sizes and higher quality at the same time, reducing bandwidth and storage use.

name: Enable text compression
guideline: Web browsers often communicate with web servers in human-readable formats such as HTML, JavaScript, CSS and JSON; compressing these text responses reduces the amount of data transmitted.

name: Keep request counts low
guideline: Accessing a web page usually retrieves an HTML file from the web server, which may then reference many additional resources the browser has to download; keeping the number of such requests low reduces network energy use.

name: Leverage pre-trained models and transfer learning
guideline: Fine-tune existing pre-trained models instead of training from scratch to dramatically reduce the compute, energy, and time required for model development.

name: Minimize main thread work
guideline: Long-running JavaScript on the browser's main thread underutilises multi-core CPUs; offloading heavy computations to Web Workers or server-side implementations reduces energy consumption.

name: Minimize the total number of deployed environments
guideline: Each additional deployed environment has an increasing energy impact, which in turn creates more emissions, so it is important to understand the necessity of each environment and its environmental impact.

name: Optimize agent orchestration to reduce unnecessary model calls
guideline: Design agentic AI workflows to minimise redundant model invocations and unnecessary compute through caching, conditional logic, and efficient orchestration patterns.

name: Optimize data storage formats for AI training and inference
guideline: Use efficient storage formats, compression, and indexing strategies for AI datasets and embeddings to reduce storage footprint, data transfer, and retrieval compute.

name: Optimize image size
guideline: Ideally, stored pixel dimensions are exactly the same as, or smaller than, the display size in pixels so that no bandwidth or storage space is wasted on oversized images.

name: Reduce transmitted data
guideline: From an energy-efficiency perspective, it is better to minimize the size of the data transmitted so that less energy is required because the network traffic is reduced.

name: Remove unused CSS definitions
guideline: CSS files are complex and require energy-intensive parsing and processing; each added CSS definition increases the amount of time and processing power needed, so unused rules should be removed.

name: Select efficient ML frameworks and inference runtimes
guideline: Choose ML frameworks and inference runtimes that best match your hardware and workload to reduce compute overhead and improve energy efficiency.

name: Serve images in modern formats
guideline: Modern image formats can help reduce bandwidth, storage and computing requirements on the displaying device compared to legacy formats.

name: Terminate TLS at border gateway
guideline: Transport Layer Security (TLS) ensures that data passed between web servers and browsers remains private and encrypted; however, repeatedly terminating and re-establishing TLS increases CPU usage, so terminating it at the border gateway can reduce overhead.

name: Use Asynchronous network calls instead of synchronous
guideline: When making calls across process boundaries to databases, file systems or REST APIs, relying on synchronous calls can cause the calling thread to become blocked and waste resources; asynchronous calls avoid this.

name: Use compiled languages
guideline: Interpreted languages re-parse and compile code on every execution, consuming more energy than pre-compiled binaries, which perform compilation once and run more efficiently.

name: Use right-sized and energy-efficient AI models
guideline: Select and optimize AI models that are appropriately sized for the task to reduce compute, memory, and energy consumption during training and inference.

name: Use server-side rendering for high-traffic pages
guideline: Server-side rendering pre-renders templates on the server rather than the client, reducing client-side energy consumption, improving load times and network round-trips, and enabling caching benefits for high-traffic sites.

name: Delete unused storage resources
guideline: From an embodied carbon perspective, it is better to delete unused storage resources so that hardware use is efficient and the storage layer is optimised for the task.

name: Match utilization requirements of virtual machines (VMs)
guideline: It is better to have one VM running at a higher utilization than two running at low utilization rates, both in terms of energy proportionality and embodied carbon.

name: Match utilization requirements with pre-configured servers
guideline: It is better to have fewer, better-utilised pre-configured servers than many under-utilised ones, both in terms of energy proportionality and embodied carbon.

name: Optimise storage utilization
guideline: It is better to maximise storage utilisation so the storage layer is optimised for the task, both in terms of energy proportionality and embodied carbon.

name: Optimize average CPU utilization
guideline: CPU usage and utilization varies throughout the day, sometimes wildly, for different computational requirements, so optimizing average CPU utilization improves overall efficiency.

name: Optimize peak CPU utilization
guideline: CPU usage and utilization varies throughout the day, sometimes wildly, for different computational requirements, so optimizing peak CPU utilization reduces the need for over-provisioned capacity.

name: Optimize power consumption for edge AI inference
guideline: Address power optimization on resource-constrained edge devices running AI inference through scheduling and thermal management techniques.

name: Remove unused assets
guideline: Unused cloud resources such as databases, storage buckets, and compute instances continue to consume energy and generate embodied carbon, so they should be identified and removed.

name: Scale down applications when not in use
guideline: Applications consume CPU even when they are not actively in use, for example through background timers, garbage collection, and health checks, so idle applications should be scaled down.

name: Scale down kubernetes applications when not in use
guideline: Dev and test Kubernetes clusters can turn off nodes outside of office hours to avoid consuming energy when workloads are not in use.

name: Scale infrastructure with user load
guideline: Most applications run without taking resource demand into consideration, resulting in underused and inefficient resources; scaling infrastructure with actual user load avoids this waste.

name: Scale Kubernetes workloads based on relevant demand metrics
guideline: Scaling workloads based on relevant demand metrics that drive application scaling, such as HTTP requests, queue length, and cloud alerting events, can help reduce resource utilization.

name: Set storage retention policies
guideline: From an embodied carbon perspective, it is better to have an automated mechanism to delete unused storage resources so that hardware use remains efficient.

name: Time-shift Kubernetes cron jobs
guideline: Carbon-aware time scheduling involves scheduling workloads, such as Kubernetes cron jobs, to execute when electricity carbon intensity is low.

name: Use carbon-aware scheduling and region selection for AI workloads
guideline: Reduce the carbon impact of AI workloads by running them in lower-carbon-intensity grid regions or during periods of high renewable energy availability.

name: Use circuit breaker patterns
guideline: If a dependent application is not reachable, all network requests against it will fail and future network requests are futile; a circuit breaker avoids wasting resources on these futile calls.

name: Scan for vulnerabilities
guideline: Implement vulnerability scanning and endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to minimize the window of opportunity for attackers and mitigate potential malicious usage of resources, reducing the unnecessary embodied carbon emissions from compromised infrastructure.

name: Use cloud native network security tools and controls
guideline: Implement network and web application firewalls to block unauthorized transmissions and filter traffic at the source, using cloud-native security tools that scale dynamically with demand to reduce unnecessary data transmission and energy consumption.

name: Use DDoS protection
guideline: Implement DDoS protection services from cloud providers to mitigate distributed denial-of-service attacks that waste environmental resources through excessive, meaningless requests.

name: Encrypt what is necessary
guideline: Data protection through encryption is a crucial aspect of security measures; however, the encryption process can be resource-intensive at multiple levels, so only encrypt what is actually necessary.

name: Match your service level objectives to business needs
guideline: If service downtime is acceptable, it is better not to strive for the highest availability but to design the solution according to real business needs; lower availability guarantees can help reduce energy consumption by using fewer infrastructure components.

name: Shed lower priority traffic
guideline: When resources are constrained during high-traffic events or when carbon intensity is high, more carbon emissions are generated; shedding lower-priority traffic avoids adding resources that introduce more embodied carbon and electricity demand.

name: Identify, assess, disclose, review, and mitigate sustainability impacts
guideline: Assess and report the planet, people, and prosperity impacts of digital projects, and plan measurable reductions to the real-world effects of their activity.

name: Understand user requirements or constraints
guideline: Identify and involve users and affected communities, and research their needs.

name: Integrate sustainability into every stage of the ideation process
guideline: Design and review sustainable branding and experiences, involve users throughout the process, and reduce unnecessary development and environmental impact through early testing and environmentally aware design.

name: Design efficient and streamlined user journeys
guideline: Design clear, efficient journeys that help users complete tasks and find content with minimal effort.

name: Design to assist and not to distract
guideline: Give users control over notifications and focus, prioritize task-relevant content, and avoid designs that distract or unnecessarily extend engagement.

name: Avoid being manipulative or deceptive
guideline: Avoid deceptive patterns, clearly label ads, respect consent for tracking, and ensure search, sharing, and discoverability practices prioritize user needs over optimization or manipulation.

name: Make deliverables understandable and reusable
guideline: Create discoverable, maintainable, and reusable documentation and code resources that support long-term understanding, reuse, and sustainability.

name: Use a design system for interface consistency
guideline: Use design systems and established patterns to ensure consistent, efficient, and sustainable interfaces through reusable components and clear maintenance practices.

name: Optimize media to reduce resource use
guideline: Include media only when it supports user needs. Manage, optimize, and load media efficiently. Ensure users have control over playback and data use.

name: Ensure animation is proportionate and easy to control
guideline: Use animation sparingly and efficiently, only when it supports understanding, while limiting performance impact and giving users control over motion.

name: Use optimized web typography
guideline: Use font strategies that minimize downloads and complexity while supporting required languages and dynamic content.

name: Avoid unwanted notifications
guideline: Send only user-requested notifications and provide clear, accessible controls for managing preferences, opt-in, and account and contact settings.

name: Reduce the impact of downloadable and physical documents
guideline: Reduce paper use through digital-first workflows, optimize and reuse accessible downloadable documents, and provide clear, user-controlled document previews and formats.

name: Involve users early in the project
guideline: Define and validate prototypes and interface components through user testing to ensure they work effectively in real-world use cases and across diverse user needs.

name: Audit and test for bugs or issues requiring resolution
guideline: Regularly audit for issues or problems, running tests at regular intervals in both simulated and real-world scenarios to ensure stability of the project.

name: Validate usability through testing and real-world usage
guideline: Monitor user feedback and real usage to evaluate feature effectiveness, and use usability testing and user research to guide ongoing improvements.

name: Provide cross-platform compatibility support
guideline: Document compatibility, avoid unnecessary obsolescence, and test across devices, systems, and network conditions.

name: Set goals based on performance and energy impact
guideline: Define performance and environmental targets, and design content with awareness of the relative energy and processing cost.

name: Minify and remove unused code
guideline: Minify code and data, and remove unused characters to reduce file size and improve loading efficiency and maintainability.

name: Modularize bandwidth-heavy components
guideline: Split large components into smaller, on-demand modules to improve loading efficiency while balancing maintainability and caching performance.

name: Avoid redundancy and duplication in code
guideline: Reduce code duplication through refactoring and reuse, ensure maintainability, and favor evolving existing solutions over rebuilding them.

name: Treat third parties the same as first parties
guideline: Minimize and carefully manage third-party services by using lightweight, user-controlled integrations that are loaded only when needed.

name: Ensure code follows good semantic practices
guideline: Use standards-compliant HTML and web platform features, and avoid unnecessary complexity or non-standard code.
